effect.description: one run of a post-commit handler, recorded so it happens at most once

handler.description: the registration that ran, by its slot id

target.description: the entity the committed change was about

kind.description: what happened to it, or `matched` where a query matched it

attempts.description: how many times the handler has been started

error.description: what the last attempt threw — kept beside a run left failed, so the record shows why

next.description: when the next attempt falls due; set means a failure that reported and is waiting out its backoff, absent means a run in progress (or one nobody has picked up)

lease_owner.description: the process currently reconciling this row

lease_token.description: that claim's token, fresh on every claim

lease_expiry.description: when the claim expires and another process may take it

lease.description: a background job held by one process at a time — its eid is derived from `name`, so two processes reaching for the same job address one row and the winner is settled by the graph's own precondition

name.description: the job being held — a sweep, a clock, a start-up pass; the eid is derived from it, so the same job is the same row in every graph

holder.description: the process running it — absent means nobody is, and the next process to ask gets it

until.description: when the hold expires; a holder still working pushes this out on a timer, and one that was killed leaves a row that expires without anything having to clean up after it

effect_check.title: Check effect runs
effect_check.description: Check recorded background actions (effects), such as sending mail after a transaction commits. Reports runs marked failed after exhausting their attempts, and runs still pending past their due time by more than the server’s threshold (10 minutes by default). An overdue run can indicate that no process is dispatching actions, even while graph writes succeed. Does not retry or mark runs failed itself; with no effect records supported by the schema, reports no findings. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.
